Subject: Encryption & KMS follow-up - FinWell / Redwood

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps on the encryption / KMS items we discussed, plus answers to the questions you raised on the bridge:

Summary from our call:
- Goals: ensure FinWell PII is protected in transit and at rest, support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for regulatory requirements, and confirm logging/retention behaviors for audit.
- Desired outcome: get you a clear options matrix (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), implementation checklist for KMS/HSM, and a proposed timeline for a pilot.

Quick answers up front:
- In-transit: All traffic to Redwood APIs is TLS 1.2+ (we default to TLS 1.3 where supported).
- At-rest: Data is encrypted at rest with AES-256; keys are managed via cloud KMS for Hosted.
- BYOK: Customer-managed keys (CMEK/BYOK) are available for Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted, we offer an enterprise BYOK pathway for customers with strict requirements — details below.
- HSM: HSM-backed key storage (e.g., CloudHSM) is supported in Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS in most cloud providers.
- Logging & retention: Audit logs, request traces, and admin logs are available. Default retention is 30 days for request logs but can be extended for enterprise accounts. We do not use customer data to train models (we’ll include this clause in the DPA).

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send the encryption overview and our SOC2 attestation (attached) + a short KMS integration checklist.
2) Neha (cc'd) from Security will add technical specifics and any constraints for Hosted vs Dedicated/Private.
3) If that looks good, we schedule a 1-hour technical deep dive with your infra/security team next week to scope the pilot.

Would next Tue (2/17) or Wed (2/18) work for a technical deep dive? Also if you can confirm whether you require HSM-backed keys vs. cloud KMS, that will help us recommend the right deployment.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

5) Attachments: can you share your SOC2 report and any encryption whitepaper? Also any guide for integrating our infra team with your KMS integration would be helpful.

Alex

Alex — thanks for the clear list. See inline answers and attached documents. Looping Neha for the deeper technical follow-up and the KMS integration doc.

1) BYOK on Hosted: short answer — for most customers BYOK is supported on Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we offer a limited BYOK path under an enterprise agreement that includes network controls and a short onboarding checklist (we do not store your CMK in our multi-tenant control plane). The Hosted BYOK path usually involves envelope encryption with a customer-supplied wrapping key in your KMS and a short-lived service key on our side; we can go into the exact flow in the technical call.

2) Plaintext storage: Hosted by default stores request/response logs for 30 days for debugging and SRE purposes. Those logs are encrypted at rest and access-controlled. We offer a "no-logs" option for sensitive customers (by contract) which disables request/response retention beyond operational traces. We also support automated redaction (PII masking) on the ingest path for tokens that match configured patterns.

3) Key rotation & audit: With BYOK (Dedicated/Private), key rotation is driven by your KMS. Redwood will call the active key for encryption/decryption; we log key usage events and can push rotation events to your SIEM (via syslog or CloudWatch) for audit. For Hosted BYOK arrangements we support a rotation window and can surface rotation events in audit logs.

4) Retention & purge: Yes — enterprise customers can configure retention windows for logs (30 days, 90 days, 1 year) and request on-demand purges for specific artifacts. We provide an API and audit trail for purge requests.

5) Attachments: please find attached:
- redwood-encryption-overview.pdf (high-level flow diagrams + Hosted/Dedicated/Private matrix)
- SOC2_Attestation.pdf (redacted attestation; full report available under NDA)
- KMS_integration_instructions.pdf (step-by-step for Dedicated/Private)

Next step: Neha — could you add the technical constraints and a recommended configuration for FinWell (given Alex's 1-year retention requirement and PII redaction needs)? Also we should lock in Wed 2/18 2pm PT for the deep dive.

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-encryption-overview.pdf; SOC2_Attestation.pdf; KMS_integration_instructions.pdf

Hi Alex — Neha from Security here. Short technical notes and recommended configuration for FinWell based on the requirements you shared.

Technical specifics:
- Hosted:
  - Encryption at rest: AES-256 with provider-managed KMS keys by default. Keys are in our cloud tenant; we do not share plaintext keys.
  - Hosted BYOK: available under enterprise contract — implemented via envelope encryption. Customer CMK stays in your KMS (we never persist CMK material in our control plane). We use a short-lived data encryption key (DEK) that is wrapped/unwrapped by your CMK.
  - Logging: request/response logs are encrypted at rest. By default request logs are retained 30 days; we can enable a no-logs mode that limits retention to operational traces only.

- Dedicated / Private (recommended for strict regs):
  - Full CMEK/BYOK support with direct KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).
  - HSM: Private deployments can be configured to use CloudHSM or customer-managed HSMs for key storage and signing. This is the recommended path if you require HSM-backed keys for compliance.
  - Key rotation: handled by customer KMS. We record key usage events and provide rotation audit logs via your preferred log sink (CloudWatch, Stackdriver, syslog).

Recommended FinWell configuration:
- Deployment: Dedicated (or Private if you need HSM). Dedicated will meet the 1-year log retention requirement and keep costs predictable.
- KMS: Use your AWS CMKs in us-west-2 and grant Redwood the minimum KMS cryptographic permissions for envelope operations.
- Logging & retention: Set request log retention to 365 days for the compliance repo. We will supply an API and a signed audit trail for purge/redaction requests.
- Data residency: Deploy Dedicated nodes in us-west-2 to satisfy residency needs. All backups and logs for that deployment will remain in the region unless you request cross-region replication.

Operational notes & next steps:
1) For the Wed 2/18 call we should have FinWell's infra/KMS engineer available (so we can validate IAM policies and create a test CMK).
2) We'll prepare a short runbook for the pilot (key creation, rotation test, purge workflow, and a small canary job to validate logs and retention).
3) I can share a sample IAM policy and the CloudFormation snippet to create the test CMK during the call.

If you want, I can also schedule a 30-minute pre-call with our infra SE (Rishi) to walk through the IAM/KMS bits.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security | Redwood Inference
neha@redwood.ai
